chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Ubayd ibn Hilal, who said: I heard Abul Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying:
"I love that the believer be muḥaddath."
I asked: "And what is the muḥaddath?"
He replied: "The one who makes things understood."

key_terms.الْمُفْهِمُ: The one who makes things understood; one who possesses and conveys clear understanding.
key_terms.مُحَدَّث: One who is spoken to or converses; here used to denote one who is articulate and clear in conveying meaning.

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'muḥaddath' mean in the context of Imam al-Rida's teaching?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) defines the ideal believer as 'al-mufhim,' emphasizing that true faith requires not just internal conviction but the intellectual capacity to articulate and clarify divine truths for others. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tafsir* (exegesis) and *bayān* (clarification) as essential duties of the learned, ensuring that religious knowledge is accessible and comprehensible to the community.
